findings.title: Historical shared-KB message files bypass a narrowed API-key allow-list
findings.scenario: An API key owns a session that previously retrieved an organization-shared KB file. After its KB allow-list changes, the chat-capable message-file route still returned the excluded file because shared-KB fallback checked organization membership but not the current key scope.
findings.reproduction: The real message-file handler returned HTTP 200 and shared-kb-image for KnowledgeBaseIDs=[another-kb], expected HTTP 403. Tenant-wide and explicitly allowed KB cases passed as controls.
findings.fix: Reapply current API-key KB scope before consuming the organization grant and binding.

invariants_checked: Original caller identity is distinct from execution tenant; grants remain exact and operation-limited.
Ownership role floors, API-key scope, live organization grants and shared-agent scope are separate gates.
File lookup requires persisted exact reference and live source binding; deleted artifact cannot be reauthorized by old answer text.
Trusted transfer/task grants bind owner, resource pair and operation; read grants cannot authorize writes.
limitations: Reviewed library source and message-file route/service/share lookup boundary; does not claim every service caller or all HTTP authorization is audited.
HTTP regression uses catalog/session/share storage doubles, not a live database or live credential.
Session-owned artifacts and chat history retain their existing session access contract.
